grid_view What is this?

Comprehensive automotive architecture at your fingertips.

This is a comprehensive public RESTful API linked to an optimized relational database detailing raw automotive architectures and live-service events from the Forza Horizon & Motorsport series.

We've covered everything from physical drivetrain profiles to dynamic seasonal milestone distributions.

api Where do I start?

We have integrated full Open API specifications out of the box. It takes seconds to target query states with automated endpoint pagination and enterprise filtering parameters.

This API acts as an open infrastructure for the global open-source automotive developer community and will never require tricky credentials for anonymous read transactions.

About Forza Open API

What is this?

This platform provides a RESTful API interface to highly detailed automotive data models built from thousands of lines of schema specifications related to the Forza franchise. We specifically cover both the open-world Horizon events and the simulation track racing Motorsport series. Using this website, application developers can easily consume clean structural data on vehicle specifications, performance tier indices, engine configurations, and dynamic seasonal log components.

What is an API?

An API (Application Programming Interface) is a contractual layer that allows mobile engineering cores, web applications, or community metrics panels to safely interact with a software application through an explicitly declared set of interfaces. In this case, the underlying platform is an optimized relational database containing thousands of automotive instances, mapped cleanly over secure web links.

A RESTful API is an architecture designed around standard HTTP request methods (GET, POST), clean separation of client-server transaction entities, and strict JSON structural returns encapsulated through distinct Data Transfer Objects (DTOs).

Aren't there 101 other Forza websites already?

Yes, and that is exactly the problem! Dozens of separate community portals and independent tool applications mean dozens of fractured, manual iterations of the exact same raw vehicle data.

When a major content drop or a new installment like Forza Horizon 6 introduces weekly live-service modifications, standalone repository architectures take weeks to update because individual engineers are forced to re-enter metadata tables across duplicate system walls.

Forza Open API resolves this overhead. By offering a single distributed source of truth, any numbers of client applications can query precise performance index metrics or reward rosters simultaneously with unified data integrity.

How much information is stored here?

A significant volume. Our persistence layer handles comprehensive normalized parameters mapping various gaming telemetry branches, including:

  • Full Physical Vehicle Metadata (Drivetrain profiles, stock aspiration types, engine variants)
  • Game-Specific Metrics (Precise performance indexes, speed mapping calibrations, launch/braking values)
  • Distinct Automotive Divisions (Hypercars, Extreme Track Toys, Classic Muscle, Modern Saloons)
  • Live-Service Seasonal Logs (Dynamic weekly challenges, PTS progression requirements, Forzathon shop states)
  • Automated Content Unlocks (Backstage passes, Wheelspin exclusive validation nodes)

So who built this?

Forza Open API was conceptualized, structured, and programmed entirely by CrusterCrew as an enterprise-grade backend engineering portfolio display.

The prompt for this asset emerged after discovering that older community endpoints (such as forza-api.tk) had completely dropped offline, leaving hobbyist mobile developers without a central database sandbox. The application is built to demonstrate how real-world enterprise architectures tackle non-bloated, data-intensive cross-relational models.

Where did you get all of this data?

The information serving this system was programmatically parsed and aggregated through custom programmatic pipelines:

  • MediaWiki Extraction Core: Bulk data ingestion targeted the native underlying MediaWiki structure powering the official Forza Fandom Wiki platform.
  • Normalizer Translation Layer: Scraped shorthand codes (e.g. div = csc or unclear rarity logs) were extracted, parsed via string dictionaries, and mapped into clean relational data layouts adhering to Third Normal Form (3NF) requirements.

What's the technology stack?

Unlike traditional monolithic architectures that handle simplistic in-memory caches, this project replicates heavy enterprise data loads through production-ready micro-infrastructures:

  • Backend Application Engine: Written in Kotlin utilizing the Spring Boot 3.x framework ecosystem with strict Data Transfer Object (DTO) isolation layers to completely prevent infinite relation looping recursions.
  • Persistence Layer Architecture: Relational entity mapping utilizes a production serverless PostgreSQL instance via Neon cloud. DDL tracking and incremental baseline operations are version-controlled strictly via Flyway Migrations on application startup.
  • Distributed Cache System: Heavy multi-criteria filtering and spec comparisons are protected through an external Redis Distributed Cache cluster via Upstash Cloud TLS, keeping core query dispatches optimized down to double-digit millisecond responses.
  • Security Ecosystem: Configured using robust stateless protocols ensuring proper route encapsulation between open queries and transactional maintenance lines.

Comprehensive automotive architecture at your fingertips.

This is a comprehensive public RESTful API linked to an optimized relational database detailing raw automotive architectures and live-service events from the Forza Horizon & Motorsport series.

We've covered everything from physical drivetrain profiles to dynamic seasonal milestone distributions.

We have integrated full Open API specifications out of the box. It takes seconds to target query states with automated endpoint pagination and enterprise filtering parameters.

This API acts as an open infrastructure for the global open-source automotive developer community and will never require tricky credentials for anonymous read transactions.

API Documentation

Welcome to the official Forza Open API documentation. Use this page to understand our endpoints, response structures, and querying parameters.

Information

This is a consumption-only API â only the HTTP GET method is available on public resources.

No authentication is required to access this API, and all resources are fully open. We utilize robust caching via Redis Upstash to guarantee rapid response times across our globally distributed nodes.

Fair Use Policy

Forza API is free and open to use. Because of this, we ask every developer to abide by our fair use policy. People not complying with the fair use policy will be subjected to rate-limiting or IP bans.

  • Locally cache resources in your own mobile app or web client whenever you request them.
  • Avoid spamming heavy complex filtering endpoints in loops.
  • If you spot data inaccuracies, please contribute via our official GitHub repository.

Pagination & Sorting

Calling any list endpoint without a specific resource ID will return a paginated list of available resources. By default, a list "page" will contain up to 20 resources.

GET https://api.forza-api.com/api/v1/vehicles?page=0&size=20&sort=modelName,desc

tune Query Parameters

Parameter Type Description
page integer The page index you want to retrieve. Starts at 0.
size integer Number of items per page. Default is 20.
sort string Field to sort by, followed by a comma and direction (e.g., id,asc or modelName,desc).

Vehicles

Vehicles are the core physical entities representing cars from the real world. They contain base attributes like engine type, chassis origin, and default drive types before game-specific tuning is applied.

Get All Vehicles

GET /api/v1/vehicles 
Mengambil data dari server...

tune Query Parameters

Parameter Type Description
manufacturerId integer Filters vehicles by the unique identifier of the manufacturer (e.g., id: 54 for Honda).
manufacturerName string Performs a case-insensitive partial match search on the manufacturer name (e.g., porsche).
startYear integer The minimum production year boundary for the dynamic search range (e.g., 1990).
endYear integer The maximum production year boundary for the dynamic search range (e.g., 2025).
driveType string (enum) Filters vehicles by layout configuration. Valid case-insensitive values: FR, MR, RR.
drivetrain string (enum) Filters vehicles by drive system layout. Valid case-insensitive values: AWD, RWD, FWD.

Get Vehicle by ID

GET /api/v1/vehicles/{id}

tune Path Parameters

Parameter Type Description
id REQUIRED integer Unique identifier of the vehicle (e.g., 28).

Search Vehicles by Model Name

GET /api/v1/vehicles/search/{model_name}

tune Path Parameters

Parameter Type Description
model_nameREQUIRED string Performs a case-insensitive partial match search on the vehicle's model name (e.g., furai).

Game Vehicles Stats

Game-specific vehicle statistics including performance ratings, handling characteristics, and classification data for each vehicle across different Forza titles.

Get All Vehicle Stats

GET /api/v1/vehicle-stats

tune Query Parameters

Parameter Type Description
vehicleid integer Filters statistics by the global real-world vehicle ID (e.g., 12).
vehiclename string Performs a case-insensitive partial match search on the car's model name (e.g., trueno).
manufacturerid integer Filters records by the specific car manufacturer's ID.
manufacturername string Filters by manufacturer name via partial query match (e.g., Ferrari).
divisionid integer Filters by the vehicle division category ID.
divisionname string Filters by division/car group names (e.g., Hypercars).
gameid integer Filters stats isolated to a specific game title (e.g., 2).
rarity string (enum) Filters by in-game acquisition rarity (LEGENDARY).
drivetype string (enum) Filters by engine layout and placement matrix (MR).
performanceclass string (enum) Filters by Performance Index (PI) Tier (S1).

Get Vehicle Stats by ID

GET /api/v1/vehicle-stats/{id}

tune Path Parameters

Parameter Type Description
id REQUIRED integer The unique identifier mapping a specific car's metrics directly to a targeted game instance (e.g., 16).

Parameter Type Description
gameId integer Filters playlist history by a specific game title instance ID (e.g., 2).

tune Path Parameters

Parameter Type Description

API Documentation

Welcome to the official Forza Open API documentation. Use this page to understand our endpoints, response structures, and querying parameters.

Information

This is a consumption-only API â only the HTTP GET method is available on public resources.

No authentication is required to access this API, and all resources are fully open. We utilize robust caching via Redis Upstash to guarantee rapid response times across our globally distributed nodes.

Fair Use Policy

Forza API is free and open to use. Because of this, we ask every developer to abide by our fair use policy. People not complying with the fair use policy will be subjected to rate-limiting or IP bans.

  • Locally cache resources in your own mobile app or web client whenever you request them.
  • Avoid spamming heavy complex filtering endpoints in loops.
  • If you spot data inaccuracies, please contribute via our official GitHub repository.

Pagination & Sorting

Calling any list endpoint without a specific resource ID will return a paginated list of available resources. By default, a list "page" will contain up to 20 resources.

GET https://api.forza-api.com/api/v1/vehicles?page=0&size=20&sort=modelName,desc

tune Query Parameters

Parameter Type Description
page integer The page index you want to retrieve. Starts at 0.
size integer Number of items per page. Default is 20.
sort string Field to sort by, followed by a comma and direction (e.g., id,asc or modelName,desc).
